uncited: DONeRF consists of two Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs): a depth oracle network and a shading network.
*   **Inputs:** Camera position, viewing direction, and optionally ground truth depth maps (or extracted depth maps for training without GT).
Train the depth oracle network for 300,000 iterations.
Use ground truth depth maps (or extracted depth maps if GT is unavailable) to create classification targets.
Use the oracle to predict sample locations for the shading network.
Train the shading network for 300,000 iterations.
**Oracle Selection:** The oracle classifies depth ranges.
*   $\text{loss}_{\text{MSE}}$ is the standard MSE between rendered and ground truth RGB.
It addresses the prohibitive computational cost of NeRF, which requires dozens of petaFLOPS.
The method was developed to enable interactive rendering (20 fps) on a single GPU.
